attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, offered as his example. Not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Faithful past-tense observation. It keeps 'apparently' and the no-product clause. 'Apparently' marks reliance on reports, not a probability hedge, so the claim can be scored. 'In 2021' is a fair rendering of 'last year' in a 2022 post.

contract.note: Reading 'last year' as the year the shutdown was reported, not the year it happened, is lenient but reasonable given 'apparently'. Without it, the October 2020 date would weigh against the claim. The product definition and the date window follow the ordinary meaning of the words.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own post confirms the October 2019 Rubik's cube demo. That is background to the claim. It says nothing about the later shutdown or about any product.
July 2021 Register report: an OpenAI spokesperson and Zaremba confirm the robotics team was disbanded. This supports the shutdown account reported in 2021.

July 2021 summary places the actual shutdown in October 2020 and lists only research outputs (a simulator, a toolkit, training techniques). It gives no explicit statement that nothing was shipped. Under the contract, the earlier date does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The shutdown part is supported: OpenAI confirmed in 2021 that it had disbanded the robotics effort, and the earlier October 2020 date does not contradict the claim under the contract. The no-product part is not established. The contract requires a release history or an explicit account showing no practical product through September 29, 2022, and none is in the packet. The packet itself records this gap. Nothing in the evidence contradicts either part, so the claim as a whole remains unresolved.
